data.cultural_impact: Arunoday holds a significant place in Indian culture as it is inspired by the Hindu deity Aruna, who is the charioteer of the sun god Surya. The name represents the new beginnings and the hope that dawn brings with the sunrise.
data.spiritual_significance: Arunoday holds deep spiritual significance in Hinduism. It symbolizes the awakening of the divine consciousness within oneself and the qualities of newness, optimism, and illumination. It encourages individuals to face challenges with renewed vigor and hope and to welcome new opportunities as they awaken to the blessings of the divine.

historical_references.reference: Arunoday was a celebrated poet and a courtier of the Vijayanagara Empire during the reign of king Krishnadevaraya (1509-1529). He is best known for his works written in Sanskrit and Telugu languages.

historical_references.reference: Arunoday was a prominent Jain scholar and philosopher of the 11th century. He wrote extensive commentaries on various Jain texts and is known for his contribution to Jain philosophy.
